Case A: A faxed Schedule II narcotic prescription is for a compounded parenteral infusion meeting the specified route and direct-administration conditions.

Case B: Staff extend that exception to any Schedule II injectable product, without checking whether it is a narcotic or a qualifying compounded infusion.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Meeting the infusion fax exception permits otherwise prohibited Schedule II refills.
Any Schedule II injectable automatically qualifies without the narcotic or compounding conditions.
The fax exception applies to any oral tablet merely because the patient also receives an infusion.
The first case must be evaluated under the specific compounded-infusion fax exception.

visible_candidates.stem:
Case A: A prescriber is about to prescribe an applicable Schedule II opioid and proposes skipping the required PMP check because the pharmacy will submit dispensing data later.

Case B: Staff conclude that gabapentin's inclusion in dispensing reports automatically places it in every specifically enumerated opioid or benzodiazepine query category.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Reporting inclusion alone does not establish every other category-specific query trigger.
Holding a pharmacist license exempts the person from duties arising when legally prescribing.
Drug schedule and opioid or benzodiazepine classification are separate facts relevant to the rule.
Later pharmacy reporting does not fulfill the prescriber's applicable pre-prescribing query obligation.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts prescription for buprenorphine-naloxone is written for opioid use disorder. Which statement best connects the drug's status to the state quantity framework?

choices.text: The naloxone component makes the entire product noncontrolled.
Any opioid-related product is Schedule II and may not have refills.
The product remains Schedule III and may qualify for the Massachusetts 90-day OUD pathway.
The product becomes Schedule VI after its first dispensing.

visible_candidates.stem: During final verification, a new community pharmacy has an incident log but no process for cause analysis or prevention. What is missing?

choices.text: A complete CQI program that detects, documents, assesses, and prevents quality-related events.
Keep the incident log alone; documentation is the entire CQI obligation.
Wait for a serious-injury report before reviewing system causes.
Delegate prevention planning to the software vendor.
Replace CQI with an annual controlled-substance inventory.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is preparing for renewal. In the first calendar year of the two-year renewal cycle, she completed 24 contact hours. In the second calendar year, she has completed 16 contact hours. Her pharmacy-law and home-study requirements are otherwise satisfied. What is the best way to address the remaining CE requirement?

choices.text: Renew now because the Board looks only at the combined 40-hour total for the two-year cycle.
Complete 4 more contact hours in the second calendar year because the 20-hour minimum applies to each calendar year.
Complete only additional pharmacy-law hours; the annual total no longer matters once the law requirement is met.
Ask the CE provider to redate 4 first-year credits so they count in the second calendar year.
Repeat all 20 second-year hours because completing more than 20 hours in the first year invalidates the surplus-year record.

visible_candidates.stem: A patient returns an unopened bottle that a Massachusetts pharmacy dispensed in error. The product appears intact. Which actions are required or permitted for the returned medication? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accept the return because it was previously dispensed in error by the pharmacy.
Do not place the returned medication back into dispensing inventory merely because the container is unopened.
Segregate or quarantine the returned medication and handle its disposition under the pharmacy's required return/disposal process.
Keep the returned medication out of active dispensing inventory while it awaits proper disposition.
Dispense the returned bottle to another patient after a pharmacist visually inspects the seal.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a valid oxycodone Schedule II prescription for 30 tablets but has only 12 tablets in stock. The patient wants the full prescribed quantity; the pharmacy dispenses 12 solely because it cannot supply the rest. Four days later the remaining stock arrives. What is the controlling federal consequence?

choices.text: The balance may be dispensed within 30 days because every Schedule II partial fill uses the patient-requested 30-day pathway.
The pharmacy may treat the remaining 18 tablets as a refill because the original total quantity was not dispensed.
The remaining 18 tablets may be transferred to another pharmacy once the original pharmacy receives stock.
The ordinary 72-hour shortage-remainder period has passed, so further quantity generally requires prescriber notification and a new prescription.
The original pharmacy may dispense the balance at any time before the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period ends.

visible_candidates.stem: During a Board-readiness walkthrough, a Massachusetts community pharmacy that dispenses Schedule II through V prescriptions has no prescription lock boxes for sale and no notice about them near the pharmacy counter. The manager says patients can buy lock boxes online instead. What is the best compliance assessment?

choices.text: The pharmacy complies because online retail availability satisfies the pharmacy's obligation.
Only pharmacies that dispense more than a threshold number of opioids must carry lock boxes.
The pharmacy needs only a verbal counseling script; physical availability and signage are optional.
The store should make prescription lock boxes available for sale and display the required notice on or near the pharmacy counter.
The requirement applies only to institutional pharmacies, not community pharmacies.

visible_candidates.stem: A pharmacist discovers that an improper warfarin dispensing caused a patient to be hospitalized, and the facts meet the serious-injury reporting criteria in 247 CMR 20.02(1). Which statements correctly distinguish the duties triggered by this same event? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist’s initial QRE documentation remains subject to the 24-hour discovery-or-notification clock.
The seven-business-day Board reporting period is measured from the date the prescription was originally written.
The manager of record must report the qualifying improper dispensing within seven business days of discovery of the related serious injury or death.
Completing the QRE record eliminates the separate serious-event report because both rules concern the same dispensing error.
The event can trigger both CQI documentation and the separate serious-event reporting pathway because the rules have different purposes and clocks.

visible_candidates.stem: A pharmacy’s software marks an alprazolam prescription for deletion seven months after it was issued because the prescription can no longer be used for refills. The pharmacy has no separate serious-event record tied to this prescription. What is the best response under Massachusetts record-retention law?

choices.text: Delete it because the end of a refill-use window automatically ends every record-retention duty.
Keep the controlled-substance prescription for the required two-year retention period; refill usability and record retention are different clocks.
Delete it if the prescriber confirms that no more refills will be authorized.
Keep it for five years because every controlled-substance prescription uses the serious-event record period.
Retention is unnecessary once the pharmacy has scanned the prescription into an electronic profile.

visible_candidates.stem: A pharmacy filled a prescription, but the patient never picked it up and the medication never left the pharmacy's control. Staff want to return the tablets to inventory by pouring them back into the manufacturer's stock bottle. What is the appropriate Massachusetts approach?

choices.text: The medication cannot be returned to stock once the prescription has been prepared and a patient-specific label has been applied.
The medication may be returned to stock under pharmacy policy in an appropriately identified return-to-stock container, without commingling it with manufacturer stock.
The medication may be poured into the manufacturer stock bottle because it never left the pharmacy or reached the patient.
The medication must be dispensed to another patient promptly or destroyed because prepared prescriptions cannot remain available for later reuse.
The medication may be returned to the manufacturer stock bottle after the first patient identifying information is removed from pharmacy records.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts provider submitted a program approval request 20 days before the planned presentation date and the Executive Director's designee denied it. The provider wants to challenge the denial. Which statement correctly describes the position?

choices.text: The submission was timely, so the denial can only have been substantive.
The provider may appeal to the full Board by written petition within 30 days of the notice of denial.
The provider must resubmit rather than appeal, because a designee's decision is unreviewable.
The provider may appeal only if it holds current ACPE accreditation.
The provider must appeal within 30 days of the planned presentation date.

visible_candidates.stem: A single incident at a Massachusetts pharmacy implicates both the pharmacist on duty and the pharmacy's own operations. The pharmacy argues the Board must choose one target. How should that argument be evaluated?

choices.text: It fails, because the Board may take disciplinary action against the pharmacist and the pharmacy alike.
It succeeds, because a single incident supports only a single disciplinary action.
It succeeds unless the Board first refers the matter to the Attorney General.
It succeeds, because entity credentials are disciplined only by the Department of Public Health.
It fails only where the pharmacist on duty is also the pharmacy's Manager of Record.

visible_candidates.stem: An authorized pharmacist practising collaborative drug therapy management in a Massachusetts community pharmacy is asked during an inspection to produce the collaborative practice documents. Which statements about what this pharmacist is required to hold are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must hold the signed original rather than a copy.
A copy of the current collaborative practice agreement must be maintained.
Copies of the current patient referral and patient consent must be included.
The documents must be maintained in the primary practice setting.
The documents must be readily retrievable when they are requested.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement will lapse at the end of this month and will not be renewed. The pharmacist plans to write to each affected patient in the week after the lapse, explaining that the arrangement has ended and how their therapy will be continued. Which duty has already been missed?

choices.text: None; written notice after the lapse discharges both of the duties owed.
Notice to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy in advance of the lapse.
Notice to each affected patient's other prescribers in advance of the lapse.
A written variation of the agreement extending it beyond the lapse date.
Arranging an uninterrupted continuation of therapy before the lapse.

visible_candidates.stem: At one Massachusetts pharmacy a patient refuses to give any allergy history after being asked on three separate visits. At another, a patient is never asked because the queue is long. Both patient profiles are incomplete in exactly the same respect. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both pharmacies are compliant, because the standard is only reasonable effort.
Both pharmacies are in breach, because the profile has to be complete.
Compliance turns on whether the missing history was clinically significant.
The first pharmacy made a reasonable effort and is compliant on these facts.
The second pharmacy made no effort at all and is not compliant.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist and a physician working in the same clinic each point to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9 as their authority to hold and give a controlled substance. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The section authorises possession of what is reasonably required for patient treatment.
It authorises administration, or causing administration under direction by a nurse.
The pharmacist appears in the section on the same footing as the physician.
The pharmacist appears only as limited by other named provisions.
Registration under section 7 is unnecessary where the practitioner acts in good faith.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's computerized system cannot show what it previously dispensed to a patient until an overnight batch runs, so at the counter the pharmacist cannot see the patient's earlier fills. The pharmacy says its staff always ask patients thoroughly about their history. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Thorough questioning satisfies the retrieval requirement, since the goal is the same.
The retrieval requirement is measured by reasonable effort, as the content duty is.
The system must allow immediate retrieval when the prescription is presented.
A pharmacy may rely on the overnight batch if it documents the limitation.
Institutional sterile compounding pharmacies are outside these requirements.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy rebrands and begins trading under a new name on 1 June. The licence holder, the premises and the ownership are all unchanged. The manager plans to mention the new name in the pharmacy's next annual renewal filing in November. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: Nothing further, since the licence holder and premises are unchanged.
Notice at the next renewal, which is what the regulation contemplates.
Written notice to the Board within 14 days, with authorizing documentation.
Written notice to the Board within 90 days, as for a change of location.
A fresh licence application, the old trading name having been surrendered.

visible_candidates.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist properly counted several courses toward last year's continuing education requirement. Eighteen months after completing the earliest course, the Board selects the pharmacist for a random audit. Which statements correctly describe the pharmacist's documentation duties? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must retain acceptable documentation for at least two years from each course's completion date.
The pharmacist must produce the documentation when the Board requests it during the random audit.
The documentation must identify the provider and participant and include the program title or number, completion date, and hours awarded.
The two-year retention period begins at the end of the biennial pharmacist-registration cycle.
The pharmacist's renewal attestation replaces the underlying course records once the hours have been credited.

visible_candidates.stem: Without patient authorization or another identified legal basis, a pharmacist sends a patient's complete medication profile through an encrypted portal to the patient's employer. The employer requested the profile for a workplace wellness review. Which statement best applies the Massachusetts licensee confidentiality duty?

choices.text: Encryption makes the transmission permissible because confidentiality duties address only accidental public exposure.
The pharmacist violates the affirmative confidentiality duty by sending the profile to an unauthorized recipient, despite using a secure channel.
The disclosure is permissible because an employer may request any medication information connected with a wellness program.
No confidentiality issue exists unless the employer later forwards the profile to someone else.
The duty is satisfied whenever the pharmacy protects its stored copy of the profile from unauthorized access.

visible_candidates.stem: A pharmacist lawfully administers an eligible medication under the applicable Massachusetts pathway. A temporary system outage prevents immediate electronic transmission of the administration record, so the pharmacist sends it to the prescriber at the next practical opportunity after service is restored. How should the timing language in the current Department guidance be characterized?

choices.text: It is a statutory SHALL deadline that automatically invalidates the administration under Massachusetts law if the record is not transmitted immediately.
It is nonmandatory guidance strongly encouraging transmission as soon after administration as practical, not a validity condition.
It prohibits any administration unless the prescriber confirms receipt of the record in advance.
It makes prescriber communication entirely irrelevant once the medication has been administered.
It requires transmission by the end of the same calendar day without regard to practical system limitations.

visible_candidates.stem: A patient returns a liquid medication that the pharmacy had correctly dispensed. The patient reports that it developed unexpected particles before the labeled expiration date, and the pharmacist reasonably suspects contamination. Which actions or conclusions are required under the Massachusetts return rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accept the returned medication even though the original dispensing was not erroneous.
Decline the return because a pharmacy must accept only medications that it dispensed in error.
Keep the returned medication out of active inventory and quarantine it from usable stock.
Dispose of the returned medication through the appropriate process rather than redispensing it.
Treat the return like an ordinary nondefective therapy-change return, for which acceptance is always mandatory.

visible_candidates.stem:
A pharmacy posts its Notice of Privacy Practices but gives every employee the same electronic-record login. It cannot identify which employee opened a patient record.

Which change most directly addresses the described electronic safeguard weakness? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A common login restricted to licensed staff with no individual log.
One workstation password and a signed privacy-notice receipt.
Individual authentication, role-based permissions, and an access log.
A shared password changed weekly and a printed staff roster.

visible_candidates.stem:
A covered pharmacy receives a valid patient request for access to an ordinary designated record set. No ground for denial applies. By day 25, it knows it cannot act within the initial 30-calendar-day period.

What is required to use the permitted extension? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Wait until day 30 has passed, then begin an automatic 30-business-day extension.
Use successive 30-day extensions if a written explanation is sent each month.
Send written reasons and a completion date before the initial 30 days end.
Ask the records vendor to restart the clock when it receives the forwarded request.

visible_candidates.stem:
A pharmacy's retention policy applies its general two-year prescription-record minimum to every document, including HIPAA-required policies and authorizations. No longer state requirement is being disputed in this scenario.

Which correction is necessary? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Use six years as the federal rule for every kind of medical record.
Retain authorizations only until the next prescription is dispensed.
Use the applicable six-year period for required HIPAA documentation.
Destroy privacy policies when a newer version becomes effective.
